directAnswer: FSR (FidelityFX Super Resolution) can work on Nvidia GPUs, but performance and quality may vary compared to AMD GPUs, as it is optimized for AMD's architecture.
summary: FSR is compatible with Nvidia GPUs, but users may experience different results in terms of image quality and performance.

sections.heading: Compatibility with Nvidia GPUs
sections.body: FSR is designed to be a cross-platform solution, meaning it can run on various hardware, including Nvidia GPUs. However, the implementation may not be as optimized as it is on AMD hardware.

sections.heading: Performance Considerations
sections.body: While FSR can enhance frame rates on Nvidia GPUs, users may notice artifacts or lower image quality in certain scenarios compared to using native resolution or AMD's own solutions.

steps.title: Check Game Compatibility
steps.detail: Ensure the game you want to use FSR with supports the feature, as not all games implement it.

steps.title: Enable FSR in Game Settings
steps.detail: Navigate to the graphics settings of the game and look for the FSR option to enable it. The exact path may vary by game.

steps.title: Adjust FSR Settings
steps.detail: Select the desired FSR quality level (Performance, Balanced, or Quality) based on your preference for performance versus visual fidelity.

faqs.question: Will FSR improve performance on my Nvidia GPU?
faqs.answer: Yes, FSR can improve performance by rendering at a lower resolution and upscaling, but the extent of improvement varies by game and system configuration.

faqs.question: Is FSR better than DLSS on Nvidia GPUs?
faqs.answer: DLSS generally offers better image quality due to its AI-driven approach, but FSR is more widely compatible across different hardware.

faqs.question: Do I need to update my drivers for FSR to work?
faqs.answer: While FSR itself does not require specific drivers, it's always a good practice to keep your GPU drivers updated for optimal performance.

caveats: FSR may not deliver the same level of image quality on Nvidia GPUs as it does on AMD GPUs due to architectural differences.
